facts.statement: The genus Theriosuchus was first described by Richard Owen in 1879.
Fossils of Theriosuchus date from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous periods.
Theriosuchus lived in Europe, Southeast Asia, and western North America during the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Theriosuchus is an extinct genus of atoposaurid neosuchian from Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous of Europe (Hungary & southern England), Southeast Asia (Thailand) and western North America (Wyoming)

facts.statement: Fragmentary records of Theriosuchus exist from the Middle Jurassic and Early Cretaceous in China, Morocco, and Scotland.
facts.quote: with fragmentary records from Middle Jurassic and Early Cretaceous sites in China, Morocco, and Scotland.

facts.statement: Three valid species of Theriosuchus are recognized: T. pusillus from southern England, T. grandinaris from Thailand, and T. morrisonensis from North America.
facts.quote: Three valid species are currently recognized: Theriosuchus pusillus from southern England, T. grandinaris from Thailand, and T. morrisonensis from the Morrison Formation of North America.

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis suggests Theriosuchus is a neosuchian related to Paralligatoridae rather than Atoposauridae.
facts.quote: Theriosuchus was previously assigned to Atoposauridae, but a 2016 cladistic analysis recovered it as a neosuchian more closely related to members of the family Paralligatoridae than to atoposaurids.

facts.statement: The species T. ibericus and T. symplesiodon were moved from Theriosuchus to the genus Sabresuchus.
facts.quote: Two species previously assigned to this genus, Theriosuchus ibericus and T. symplesiodon, have been reassigned to the new genus Sabresuchus.

facts.statement: The species T. guimarotae was reassigned from Theriosuchus to the genus Knoetschkesuchus.
facts.quote: On the other hand, Theriosuchus guimarotae from Portugal has been reassigned to Knoetschkesuchus.

facts.statement: The genus authority for Theriosuchus is Owen, 1879.
Theriosuchus is classified within the family Atoposauridae.
Theriosuchus is an extinct genus of basal crocodilian from the Early Cretaceous of Asia and England.
facts.quote: Theriosuchus es un género extinto de mesoeucrocodilio atoposáurido del Cretácico Inferior de Asia y Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The known species are T. pusillus from England (Owen, 1879) and T. grandinaris from Thailand (Lauprasert et al., 2011).
facts.quote: Las dos especies conocidas son T. pusillus de Inglaterra (Owen, 1879), y T. grandinaris del Berriasiense-Barremiense de Tailandia (Lauprasert et al., 2011).

facts.statement: Theriosuchus was a common terrestrial basal crocodilian in Europe during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Theriosuchus fue un mesoeucrocodilio terrestre común en Europa durante el Cretácico.

facts.statement: Theriosuchus was one of the few basal crocodilians present in Laurasia during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Fue uno de los pocos mesoeucrocodilios basales presentes en Laurasia durante el Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the genus name as Theriosuchus, attributed to Owen in 1878.
The time range for Theriosuchus is estimated from 168.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Maastrichtian (168.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 44 recorded fossil occurrences of Theriosuchus in the Paleobiology Database.
